Scaling: log1p and StandardScaler fitted ONCE on the full dataset; the resample draws rows of that matrix

Estimand: Silhouette(K=4) - Silhouette(K=3), both fitted on the SAME resample
Scaling: log1p and StandardScaler fitted ONCE on the full dataset; the resample draws rows of that matrix
Evaluated_rows: the RESAMPLE itself, duplicates included. Duplicated customers sit at distance zero from each other, which raises cohesion, so this level is optimistic; the paired difference cancels most of that but not all of it. The out-of-bag check in rev2_paired_bootstrap.py exists for this reason
Interval: percentile: the 2.5th and 97.5th of the 100 differences
Seeds: numpy default_rng(42) for the indices; KMeans random_state=42+b
Olist: NO - UCI only. rev2_paired_bootstrap.py extends it to Olist and to three other datasets

Interval: percentile: the 2.5th and 97.5th of the 100 differences

Interval: percentile: the 2.5th and 97.5th of the 100 differences

Estimand: Silhouette(K=4) - Silhouette(K=3) and DBI(K=4) - DBI(K=3) on the same resample, per dataset; and for UCI the same differences evaluated only on the customers the resample did NOT draw
Scaling: log1p and StandardScaler fitted ONCE on the full dataset; the resample draws rows of that matrix (kept identical to the published protocol so the numbers are comparable)

Evaluated_rows: both: the resample itself, AND the out-of-bag customers for UCI, which share no row with the fitting set

Olist: YES - and its Silhouette is an ESTIMATE on a 10,000-point subsample (n=93,358 > the 20,000 exact threshold in rfm_scoring.py). Within one resample the same subsample serves both K values, so the pairing is exact even though the level is an estimate
